summary.headline: Gland Pharma Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to Rs 18,336 mn, adjusted EBITDA margin 27%, with CDMO up 31% to Rs 8,227 mn.
summary.overview: Gland Pharma reported Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 18,336 mn (+23% YoY), with reported EBITDA of Rs 4,804 mn (+53%) and adjusted EBITDA of Rs 5,030 mn (27% margin, after Rs 226 mn non-cash ESOP-type expense). PAT rose 58% YoY to Rs 2,908 mn. CDMO grew 31% to Rs 8,227 mn (about 45% of revenue) and critical injectables grew 18% to Rs 10,109 mn. Cenexi posted a planned shutdown-driven EBITDA loss of EUR 6 mn on EUR 41 mn revenue, and management guided Cenexi to return to profit from Q3. Management kept FY27 growth guidance at 15% in constant currency and announced additional capex, including a Rs 1,000 crore greenfield block at Vizag.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 7,092 mn in H1 FY26
vs 65% in Q1, attributed to lower Cenexi revenue
Elevated by Cenexi losses not tax-benefited

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 8,227 mn (+31% YoY, ~45% of revenue); H1 Rs 17,142 mn (+25%, ~47% of revenue). Management said CDMO margins are about 5-10% better than the injectables business.

segments.name: Critical injectables
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 10,109 mn (+18% YoY); H1 Rs 19,197 mn (+18%). Growth came from recent launches, new customers and higher volumes.

segments.name: United States
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 11,795 mn (+42% YoY); H1 Rs 21,605 mn (+37%). Four products launched in the quarter. Management said ex-Cenexi US growth was similar to the reported figure.

segments.name: Europe and other regulated markets
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 4,110 mn (+23% YoY); H1 Rs 8,598 mn (+17%).

segments.name: Rest of world
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 2,044 mn, hit by supply and tender dynamics, including a delayed NUPCO (Saudi Arabia) tender award.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 387 mn; management described it as a small part of the business.

segments.name: Cenexi (Europe)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue EUR 41 mn (vs EUR 40 mn a year ago) with EBITDA loss of about EUR 6 mn from planned annual shutdowns. Management guided to profitability from Q3 and said the focus is cost and efficiency rather than revenue growth.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance kept at 15% on a constant-currency basis; management said it is hard to predict the currency effect.
Cenexi expected to return to profitability from Q3 FY27; revenue growth expected to be minimal while cost reduction is prioritised.

Senexi FY27 guidance (previously high-single-digit EBITDA margin on about EUR 200 mn revenue) was said to still be on track. Management said H2 was already planned to be lower; the implied H2 is about EUR 111 mn at 18-20% margin, and the guidance will be updated if it changes.
Management said new launches would add about 6-7% to growth, and CDMO is expected to keep growing faster than the core business.
Management did not give guidance on the CDMO tech-transfer or GLP-related revenue contribution.
capex_capacity: Existing Rs 2,000 crore expansion programme is on track: additional lines for ophthalmic products, a new BFS line, and oncology and sterile capacity using isolator technology.

Brownfield expansion at the Vizag (Pashamylaram) site: about Rs 1,000 crore for three isolator-based lines, with commercial operations from FY30 per the transcript (the Q&A also referenced two years to commercialisation).

Greenfield project at Vizag SEZ: land acquired; the capex amount is not yet finalised and board approval is expected next quarter. Management said the programme would take about four years and that the first phase is about Rs 3,000 crore in total with 300-400 mn units of added capacity.
Liquid orals utilisation is about 92%. Oncology and bag capacity is constrained, and management has deferred some planned shutdowns because of demand.
Cenexi plans (new viral and lyophilisation block and a high-speed fill line at Fontenay) remain on track.
demand_pricing: Management said the US growth was driven by new launches and new CDMO business, with no lumpiness expected.
Management expects CDMO growth to continue to outpace the core injectables business.
R&D spend is rising for complex injectables; management said margins would be maintained.
Management said the Saudi NUPCO tender has still not been announced; Gland has bid on about 13 products and expects to win some when it opens.
India strategy: in-licensing innovative products from China for the Indian market, not generics.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year outlook for the US, Europe and rest of world, given currency moves?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth guidance is unchanged at 15% constant currency. US growth is driven by launches and CDMO and is not lumpy. Rest-of-world is expected to improve once the Saudi tender opens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total capex over four years, including the greenfield project?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 2,000 crore for existing lines plus Rs 1,000 crore for the new brownfield block, so about Rs 3,000 crore in the first phase. Greenfield amount to be announced next quarter. Management said the total could reach about Rs 5,000 crore including greenfield, and that the first phase adds 300-400 mn units.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for hiring a China-based CIO and business development head?
qa_highlights.answer: The CIO will do global acquisitions, with a focus on US biologics, and will also look at licensing and technology from China. Business development will focus on bringing innovative products from China to India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin split between CDMO and the core business? Is Cenexi in CDMO?
qa_highlights.answer: CDMO margins are about 5-10% better than the injectables business. Cenexi revenue is included in CDMO.

qa_highlights.question: Is Senexi FY27 guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the lower H2 number was already planned, and the earlier estimate is on track. It will update if anything changes.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the R&D increase and the sequential gross margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is rising for complex products and in-licensing, and management said margins would be held. The gross margin decline to 63.5% was due to lower-margin Cenexi revenue.

risks_watch: Cenexi is still loss-making in Q2 and depends on the Q3 profit recovery; the FY27 Senexi guidance implies a sharp H2 margin improvement.
Capacity is tight at key sites. Missing the timing on the brownfield and greenfield projects, or the US inspection outcome for the new bag line, could constrain revenue.
Currency: about 80% of revenue is exported, and management said constant-currency growth cannot be measured precisely.
Rest-of-world revenue depends on the timing of the Saudi NUPCO tender, which is still delayed.
Rising R&D (6% of Q2 revenue) and a larger capex plan could pressure margins and cash.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, capacity and CDMO growth, while cautious on rest-of-world timing and on Cenexi's near-term profitability. Management was non-committal on the greenfield capex amount and the CDMO and GLP product revenue contribution, and deferred those details to later updates.

So this is a combination of what all you mentioned. One is of course as you've been saying you want to acquire something in US on the biologic side.
So the growth will be overall, as you have seen for this quarter as well, like across Europe and US market.
